semantics.behavioral: Every stage and listed fact is required within a route. Enabled routes are alternatives for one objective. Steps progressively reveal the finite model.
semantics.prevention: Each eligible control in a route can break it when applied prospectively. A minimum cut is the smallest eligible set hitting all enabled routes.
semantics.detection: A placement names a possible signal type for that route. Placement intersection alone does not confer collector coverage or evidence.
semantics.evidence: Effect requires an independent outcome witness and objective scope. Origin requires a scoped initiating principal. Causality requires effect, origin and exact binding. Intended authorization is assessed for a causally linked operation.
semantics.provenance: Mechanism support describes the source contribution. All route compositions and cut results are research models. Lab counts remain in the study receipts.

M.name: Remove direct read grant
M.eligibility: Block all modeled live references before the read. Earlier copies remain readable.

Mw.name: Remove direct write grant
Mw.eligibility: Block live write references before use. Earlier state changes require separate recovery.

F.name: Verify and enforce direct read policy
F.eligibility: Assumes subject-aware enforcement across all four direct routes, including applicable mapped and descriptor reads.

N.name: Restrict relevant namespace reach
N.eligibility: Deny the required eligible context before use.

R.name: Fix leaked runtime reference
R.eligibility: Remediate before the affected lifecycle request.

G.name: Fix device integration
G.eligibility: Remediate before setup exposes the host resource or socket.

A.name: Remove conventional daemon grant
A.eligibility: Applies to the configured grant. Device setup can create another route.

J.name: Enforce daemon job authorization
J.eligibility: Requires reliable origin and enforcement for the named jobs, including device-derived daemon reach.

C.name: Fix CRI copy handling
C.eligibility: Act before a workload-readable copy is created.

S.name: Remediate or isolate the affected shim
S.eligibility: Include vulnerable instances still running after a package upgrade.

H.name: Fix cgroup authorization
H.eligibility: Act before the affected cgroup operation.

V.name: Remove the affected cgroup v1 surface
V.eligibility: Removes a required precondition for the modeled cgroup route.

B.name: Fix runtime lifecycle integrity
B.eligibility: Act before replacement. Previously altered host binaries require recovery.

K.name: Fix the shared-kernel flaw
K.eligibility: Act before exposure to the affected interface.

P.name: Fix privileged write redirection
P.eligibility: Act before vulnerable setup. The resulting host write has a separate recovery path.

L.name: Enforce host consumer input policy
L.eligibility: Hypothesis for the exact scheduler or service input and consumer.

T.name: Enforce local trust-store policy
T.eligibility: Assumes complete mediation through relevant local trust resolution.

U.name: Enforce configured publisher authorization
U.eligibility: Covers this publisher only. Other providers require separate treatment.

objectives.name: Protected host data
objectives.objective: Obtain one designated host data version. The receiver starts without that version.
objectives.startingScope: Obtain one designated host data version. The receiver starts without that version.

optionalFacts.label: Daemon can complete the host-reading job
optionalFacts.description: This enables the modeled interaction, before any receipt evidence.

objectives.otherExplanations: A Kubernetes Secret response can explain possession of other credentials. Bind the actual source version before counting it as acquisition of this host object. An approved backup can read the same host file.
objectives.modelLimit: The cut applies to the displayed routes and this exact data version. Existing copies and unmodeled providers can require separate controls.

walkthrough.title: Find the protected object
walkthrough.prompt: Sysdig reported host-file output after a workload used Docker management access. First ask what a direct read would establish. A host mount alone establishes exposure.

walkthrough.title: Follow the runtime job
walkthrough.prompt: An authenticated request can identify the requester. Add a terminal result and a link to the exact recipient before crediting a mediated read.

walkthrough.title: Follow the copy
walkthrough.prompt: containerd disclosed a route that materialized read-only host copies. Select the local read and look for the original version. Matching content can come from a stale copy.

walkthrough.title: Try the device route
walkthrough.prompt: Wiz showed a read-only host mount still gave access to a socket. Enable both prerequisites for that composed route, then compare the configured grant with job authorization.

routes.name: Direct host mapping
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Completed read bound to the source version and recipient.

routes.name: Namespace-mediated read
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Target namespace and resulting actor bound to the completed read.

routes.name: Leaked runtime reference
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Resolved reference and completed read of the exact source version.

routes.name: Device setup exposes host data
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Observed host mapping and completed acquisition tied to the workload.

routes.name: Configured daemon delegation
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Exact job terminal and delivery to the authenticated requester.

routes.name: Device setup followed by delegation
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Authenticated job, exact protected read, and requester-bound delivery.

routes.name: Runtime materializes a copy
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Protected source version bound to the copied object and recipient read.

objectives.name: Host execution
objectives.objective: Execute attacker-controlled user-space code under host authority. The attacker starts without that execution.
objectives.startingScope: Execute attacker-controlled user-space code under host authority. The attacker starts without that execution.

optionalFacts.label: The workload can write this host input
The configured host consumer would execute the new definition
optionalFacts.description: Both scheduler or service conditions must hold.

objectives.otherExplanations: An external management caller can launch a host-authorized workload. An approved package update can replace the same binary. A nearby launch may consume a clean version. Shared-writable artifact execution has its own catalog contract.
objectives.modelLimit: These cuts omit takeover of an already host-authorized process or workload and unenumerated host scheduler or service inputs.

walkthrough.title: Qualify the context
walkthrough.prompt: A namespace move can explain how a route begins. Check the resulting actor and what authority it actually exercised.

walkthrough.title: Check what the controller did
walkthrough.prompt: Compare a daemon, an abstract shim, and a cgroup-mediated action. A request, a setting change, and a host action need separate evidence.

walkthrough.title: Match the launch to the changed generation
walkthrough.prompt: The runc lifecycle disclosure describes host runtime overwrite. For the execution claim, check that a later action consumed the affected generation.

walkthrough.title: Test the model boundary
walkthrough.prompt: Add a writable scheduler or service input when both prerequisites hold. Check which control must change and which routes still reach the objective.

routes.name: Namespace-qualified execution
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Target context and relevant process lifetime tied to actual execution.

routes.name: Configured daemon delegation
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Authenticated job terminal and exact created instance tied to execution.

routes.name: Abstract shim delegation
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Shim operation and qualifying resulting host execution tied to the origin.

routes.name: Cgroup-mediated execution
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Scoped control change linked to the independently observed host action.

routes.name: Runtime binary replacement
routes.origin: New launch or existing workload lifecycle
requiredBehavioralStages: New launch or existing workload lifecycle
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Later launch consumed the exact affected generation.

routes.name: Shared-kernel isolation failure
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Qualifying user-space host action, with a witness independent of the affected kernel.

routes.name: Privileged runtime write redirected
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Later host execution is linked to the actual redirected write.

routes.name: Device setup followed by delegation
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Exact daemon-created instance is bound to an attacker-controlled host action.

routes.name: Host scheduler or service consumption
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Configured consumer executed the applicable changed definition.

objectives.name: Persistent SSH trust
objectives.objective: Make a previously untrusted key eligible for a named existing account and connection context.
objectives.startingScope: Make a previously untrusted key eligible for a named existing account and connection context.

optionalFacts.label: The modeled central publisher is configured
optionalFacts.description: This is a separate trust input.

optionalFacts.label: The actor can exercise the modeled publisher route
optionalFacts.description: Both publisher conditions must hold. An approved publication remains a competing cause.

objectives.otherExplanations: An approved rotation can change the same file. A central publisher can establish effective trust without a node escape. A later authenticated session is a separate result, and may require additional factors.
objectives.modelLimit: The local cut assumes all relevant local trust inputs are mediated. The publisher control covers only the configured publisher shown here. Other key or certificate inputs require separate treatment.

walkthrough.title: Find the trust change
walkthrough.prompt: Datadog reported SSH persistence in an external-Docker-origin campaign. For this exercise, start with a workload-origin route that changes a local trust input.

walkthrough.title: Check effective trust
walkthrough.prompt: A file write can be ineffective. Bind the exact account, key, connection context, and resolver decision. Check whether a runtime job performed the change.

walkthrough.title: Compare a configured publisher
walkthrough.prompt: Bring the central route into the threat scope only when it is configured and the actor can exercise it. Recompute the cut and keep origin separate from the destination result.

routes.name: Direct change to local trust
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Exact altered trust input linked to effective server resolution.

routes.name: Delegated change to local trust
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Delegated job targeted the exact trust input used by the server.

routes.name: Configured central publisher
routes.exactBindingRequirement: Publication is linked to the effective account and key decision.
